findings.finding: The self-invocation guard built a URL by string concatenation. `file://${path}` truncates at "#" or "?" and double-encodes "%", so the comparison against import.meta.url fails, dispatch never runs, and the process still exits 0 — every hook a silent no-op while the harness reports success.
findings.judge_reproduction: Copied the tree to /tmp/hash#dir with a paused project: the control at /tmp/normaldir printed KBD REANCHOR and exited 0; the #-path printed nothing and exited 0.
findings.disposition: ACCEPTED AND FIXED. Confirmed the divergence on four path shapes. RED test written first (fails against the old guard), then fixed.

findings.severity: CRITICAL (second-order, found while fixing the above, NOT identified by the judge)
findings.finding: pathToFileURL alone was insufficient: import.meta.url reports the REALPATH while argv[1] keeps the symlinked path. On macOS /var is a symlink to /private/var, so the two differ for anything under a temp directory. The test written for the first defect still failed after fixing it.
findings.disposition: FIXED. The guard now compares realpathSync(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) against realpathSync(process.argv[1]), which collapses both the encoding and the symlink problem.

findings.finding: The measurement checked only exit status, but the entry point exits 0 on every degradation, so a no-op dispatch would have made the numbers look BETTER while measuring nothing.
findings.disposition: ACCEPTED AND FIXED. Measurement now runs against a fixture project with a PAUSE file and asserts per-hook liveness, plus a dispatch-reachability probe for taskcompleted-kbd-receipt, which prints nothing. My first attempt assumed one shared marker for all three hooks; the check itself caught that as wrong. Mutation-verified: forcing the guard false now fails with "dispatch is not reachable".
